newsitem.title: USA: Cold, snow slow livestock movement in Iowa, Minn.
newsitem.headline: Cold, snow slow livestock movement in Iowa, Minn.

text.p: A cold, snowy weekend hampered livestock movement in parts of Minnesota and Iowa but meteorologists said the worst weather has passed.

"Anywhere from four to eight inches of snow fell there over the weekend and behind that snow this morning, you're looking at sub-zero (Farenheit) temperatures," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

"Things will get back to normal in terms of being able to transport the animals off to market in the next few days," he added. "It's going to stay cold although it will likely not be as cold in the coming days as it is this morning."
The low temperature in Sioux Falls, S.D. on Monday was 12 degrees below zero F, about 30 degrees below normal, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express.
"We had single digits (temperatures) all the way down to Kansas," Gesser said.
He said temperatures would warm gradually throughout the week with mostly dry conditions in the U.S. Plains but another storm was expected to drop more snow this weekend.
"We should have a cold week all the way into Thanksgiving (Thursday) with temperatures trying to warm up ahead of another system Friday and Saturday," Gesser said.
Palmerino said light snow was possible in the U.S. Plains on Wednesday but otherwise conditions were expected to be dry.

"We're not looking for too much in the way of additional major storms," Palmerino said. "There is the potential that we could see a little bit of light snow or flurry activity in the western Corn Belt on Wednesday, continuing into Thursday.
Snow was expected to move east across Ohio on Monday with two to four inches possible, Gesser said.
